item.evidence: WorldGlobe.jsx:94 selects any missing-feature place with Math.hypot(p.lat - at.lat, p.lng - at.lng) < 0.35 instead of testing its boundary. countries_data.py:47 places VA at 41.9,12.45. frontend/public/countries.geojson includes Italy but no VA feature. MiMundo.jsx:57-59 renders the panel for the returned code.
item.expected: R-025 (derived): clicking a tiny country opens 'that country's own information panel'; request: 'Al pulsar sobre un país se abrirá una ventana con su información'. Country identity must follow the clicked boundary, not merely proximity to another country.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: source predicts a click in central Rome (41.90,12.50), inside the supplied Italy polygon, returns VA because its coordinate distance from the VA reference is 0.05 < 0.35. Travellers selecting Italy around Rome receive Vaticano's name, status and registration action instead. The same overbroad hit area affects other microstates; selecting Italy elsewhere or using the picker is a safe recovery.
reproduction_steps: Open Mi Mundo and zoom into Rome.
Click central Rome east of Vaticano, around 41.90,12.50.
The click handler chooses VA and opens Ciudad del Vaticano, not Italia.
item.title: Clicking Rome opens Vaticano instead of Italy — tiny-country fallback captures a 0.35-degree radius

item.evidence: server.py:814 excludes only _id, user_id and comments from the shared city; :816 passes it to enrich_city, which spreads **c at :470, retaining share_token. :825 enriches a shared trip, and :826-828 strip only user_id/comments from its nested cities, retaining each city's share_token. By contrast :784 explicitly strips the token in public_view.
item.expected: R-031 (derived): the public response 'carries no owner share token, email or unshared photo'. Checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: responses exclude tokens and keep delegated access scoped to the intended resource. Explicitly project public fields for both the city and nested city records.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: source predicts signed-out share recipients receive stored sharing credentials, including independent city links inside a shared trip. A recipient can retain a separately shared city's token even when only given a trip link, then continue opening that city after the owner moves it out of the trip. Email and personal comments are excluded, but the public projection is not the promised allowed-field boundary. Scope is share-link recipients, not arbitrary account access; no runtime request was made.
reproduction_steps: Create a city, use Compartir galería, and attach it to a trip.
Share the trip and open its link signed out.
Inspect the public trip response: its nested city contains the independent city share_token.
Move the city to another trip; the recipient still has a standalone link to it. The direct public city response also echoes its own token.
item.title: Public share responses disclose city sharing credentials — public serializers return stored share_token fields

item.evidence: server.py:531 tests only {'id': data['cover_photo_id'], 'user_id': profile['user_id']}; :539-541 repeat that same check. Neither requires city_id, is_deleted=False, kind=gallery or media_type=image. :538 moves gallery trip associations before :545 stores the accepted cover. enrich_city at :468 uses that id directly, while serve_file at :712 excludes deleted files.
item.expected: R-032 (derived): validate 'the proposed cover photo against the stored gallery before moving any photo', and an invalid update leaves city, gallery and cover unchanged. A cover must be a live image in that city's gallery, not simply any file the caller owns.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: source predicts an owner's update assigning city A a deleted photo id or a photo belonging to city B succeeds, and an accompanying trip reassignment moves A's photos. A deleted photo then renders a missing cover; another gallery's photo misrepresents A. This violates the promised whole rejection of an invalid cover and requires a corrective edit; owner isolation itself is enforced.
reproduction_steps: Create two cities A and B and upload an image to B.
As the owner, submit PUT /api/cities/<A> with B's photo id as cover_photo_id and a different owned trip_id.
The handler accepts the foreign-gallery cover and moves A's photos rather than refusing the update.
Repeat with the id of a deleted owned photo: the accepted cover URL cannot be served.
item.title: City edits accept a cover from another gallery or a deleted file — validation checks ownership only

item.evidence: tiles.py:111-114 marks a missing flag incomplete and paints a cyan fallback; :76-78 returns only its bytes without caching them in _tiles. server.py:224-228 cannot distinguish that incomplete result and always sends 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=604800'. WorldGlobe.jsx:29 uses the same URL for the same tile and visited set.
item.expected: R-029 (derived): a failed flag download must not become a permanent failure and repeating the tile must try the flag again. Request: 'Que conforme voy ampliando el mundo se vean los colores en 4k'. Incomplete fallback responses must remain retryable throughout the HTTP cache path.
item.observed: Third-party integrations: if a flag download fails during render, the backend avoids its internal tile cache, but the browser/proxy is explicitly allowed to reuse the fallback JPEG for 604800 seconds (7 days). Returning to the same zoom after the provider recovers therefore need not issue another request or retry the flag. Travellers keep seeing a flat cyan visited country instead of its flag; clearing caches is not an ordinary in-app recovery. This is a source prediction, not a measured outage.
reproduction_steps: Open a visited country's globe tile while its flag provider fails.
Let the endpoint return its fallback JPEG with the current cache header.
After the provider recovers, revisit the same tile/zoom with normal browser caching.
The cached fallback can be reused for seven days without reaching the server retry logic.
item.title: A temporary flag outage leaves the globe's blue fallback cached for a week — incomplete tiles receive long-lived success headers

item.evidence: tiles.py:89 finishes _pool.map(_flag, needed); failed _flag calls return None without recording an attempt at :61-62. The subsequent loop over each polygon at :98-111 calls _flag(code) again. Each failing call has timeout=20 at :58, including repeated polygons for the same country.
item.expected: R-029 (derived): flags for visited countries on a tile are fetched in parallel so response time is not the sum of flag fetches. Checklist, Third-party integrations: delayed/unavailable dependencies need bounded, usable failure handling. Reuse the current render's prefetch results, retrying failures on a later request rather than serially during the same render.
item.observed: Performance and resource leaks: when several relevant flag requests time out, prefetch is parallel but rendering then retries those same failed requests one polygon at a time. For three intersecting countries with one polygon each and 20-second timeouts, the flag path is approximately 20 + 3×20 = 80 seconds, excluding imagery; multipart countries can add more retries. Users zooming during a flag outage wait for tiles, and requests occupy synchronous worker threads far beyond the promised parallel first render. No latency was measured.
reproduction_steps: Mark several countries in one low-zoom tile visited.
Request that tile while their flag downloads time out.
Trace the parallel prefetch completion followed by the per-polygon _flag calls.
Each failed flag is downloaded again sequentially before the fallback JPEG is returned.
item.title: Flag-provider failures still serialize long retries within each tile — failed parallel prefetches are fetched again in the polygon loop

item.evidence: server.py:52 declares the unique (user_id,country_code) index. ensure_indexes at :71-74 catches every creation exception and only logs it; startup at :946 awaits this fail-open helper. create_visited at :293-295 uses a non-atomic precheck followed by insert_one at :280.
item.expected: R-033 (derived): startup 'ensures the unique indexes it relies on' and simultaneous identical visits leave one stored record. Checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: uniqueness must be store-enforced, not only checked before insertion. Do not serve writes while that guarantee is unavailable.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: if the unique index cannot be created (for example a store containing historical duplicate visits), awaiting ensure_indexes still reports successful startup. Two new simultaneous submissions for the same user and country can both pass the precheck and persist duplicate records. Lists and passports then show duplicates; a delete removes only one record. This is conditional on an index-creation error, not a claim that the deployed database currently has one.
reproduction_steps: Start with a database where the required user_country unique index fails to build, such as a migrated collection containing duplicates.
Start the backend: the exception is logged but startup completes.
Send two simultaneous visits for a different, previously unvisited country under one account.
Both prechecks can see no record and both inserts succeed without the required index.
item.title: Backend starts without required uniqueness after an index error — startup logs and suppresses index-creation failures

item.evidence: CitySearch.jsx:14 clears res only for queries shorter than two characters; :17-18 begins a lookup without clearing res. :21 replaces res only on success, whereas :22 only sets error on failure. :38-43 continues to render the retained results and lets onSelect use them.
item.expected: Checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: pending/failure states and available controls must reflect the actual operation. R-027's failure/clearing outcome supports a usable city-search recovery. Results must correspond to the displayed query, not a previous successful query.
item.observed: UI state, navigation and interaction: after a successful Paris lookup, changing the query to Roma retains Paris buttons during the next lookup and indefinitely if it fails. The error says the service is unavailable but the results below still look selectable for Roma. Travellers can register the wrong city's name and coordinates, or must inspect and redo the selection. A new successful lookup or clearing the box is a safe recovery; stale network completions themselves are correctly guarded.
reproduction_steps: Open Añadir ciudad and search Paris; wait for results.
Replace the query with Roma without clearing it to fewer than two characters.
During the debounce/request, or if the Roma request fails, observe that the Paris result buttons remain.
Selecting a retained button submits the earlier Paris city, not a Roma result.
item.title: City lookup keeps selectable results for the previous query after a failure — new searches never clear the result state

item.evidence: create_city inserts the city at server.py:505 before :507 checks whether to mark the country visited and :508 calls add_visited. The required unique index is at :52; add_visited's insert at :280 has no DuplicateKeyError handling. AddCityDialog.jsx:41-47 treats any failed response as failure and keeps the form for retry, without the committed city id.
item.expected: R-033 (derived): concurrent identical country visits must be refused without duplicates. Checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: multi-document operations must not leave unexplained half-written state, and retries preserve operation identity. A city-plus-country save should return the saved city or fail without leaving an unacknowledged city behind.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: with the unique index working, two tabs saving different cities in the same not-yet-visited country can each insert their city and then both see no country visit. One add_visited fails on the unique key after its city is committed, producing an unhandled 500. That tab never receives the city id, never uploads its selected photos, and retry creates another city record. The loss is misleading save failure, missing attachments and duplicate travel records, recoverable through manual cleanup.
reproduction_steps: In two tabs for one account, open Añadir ciudad for two cities in an unvisited country.
In both, choose Sí, marcar país y guardar at nearly the same time.
Interleave the requests so both cities insert and both country-existence checks run before either country insert.
One country insert loses the unique-index race after its city was saved; retry the apparent failed save and see the second city record created.
item.title: Concurrent city-and-country saves report failure after saving the city — country uniqueness errors occur after an irreversible city insert

item.evidence: server.py:770 gates top-level country data on show_countries, and :776 gates top-level cities on show_cities. But :769 always returns unlocked achievements, whose progress/goal are computed from those counts (stats.py:33-43,46-47). :783-788 return enriched public trips including country_codes/countries without applying show_countries; enrich_trip supplies country names at :365.
item.expected: Request: 'Mostrar u ocultar países' and 'Mostrar u ocultar ciudades'. Checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: privacy restrictions hold across details and derived outputs, not only the primary list. Hidden countries/cities must not be disclosed through a different public projection.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: for a public profile with show_countries=false, a signed-out caller still receives the countries of each public trip and country-count achievement progress. Disabling show_cities also leaves city achievement counts visible. Thus a traveller's selected privacy controls omit the direct lists but disclose the same protected category via other response fields. Individually shared links can reasonably reveal their chosen trip, but this leak occurs on the ordinary public profile itself without using such a link.
reproduction_steps: Create travel records and a public trip; set the profile public but turn off showing countries and cities.
Open /u/<username> signed out and inspect GET /api/public/users/<username>.
Observe trip country_codes/countries and unlocked achievement progress despite privacy flags being false.
item.title: Public profiles reveal hidden country information — privacy gates are not applied to public trips or achievement payloads

item.evidence: server.py:578-579 always reuses or creates a city token and stores it; :811 authorizes a public read solely by that token. CityUpdate (:451-459) has no share/revoke field and there is no DELETE share handler in the route inventory. Trip sharing similarly stores a token at :429-430; switching is_public off in update_trip does not clear it. CityDetail.jsx:56-59 and TripDetail.jsx:54-58 expose sharing and deletion but no stop-sharing action.
item.expected: Checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: delegated/shared access must respect revocation; request: 'Cada usuario podrá decidir qué información quiere compartir' and private by default. R-031 refers to an unknown or revoked token returning none of the record. Owners need a way to invalidate a previously issued link without destroying their travel history.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: once an owner presses Compartir, the city/gallery link remains valid permanently until the city itself is deleted; making the profile private, turning off public-trip visibility, or pressing Compartir again cannot invalidate it. Travellers who accidentally share private memories or later withdraw permission cannot safely revoke access while keeping their work. This is a missing recovery capability rather than a claim that deliberately shared links should obey profile visibility.
reproduction_steps: Create a city/gallery and use Compartir galería to issue its link.
Decide to stop sharing while retaining the city and photos.
Look for a revoke/unshare action or API operation: none exists; sharing again returns the same token.
Open the original link signed out after setting the profile private: the city still loads.
item.surface: City/trip sharing controls; public share routes
item.title: Owners cannot withdraw a shared gallery or trip link without deleting their records — no token revocation operation exists

item.evidence: server.py:652 defaults private photo retrieval to 200 and :660 returns only that many without offset/cursor. PhotoGallery.jsx:38-39 never supplies a limit or requests a later page. Public city/trip queries at server.py:815 and :829 cap at 500 and return no continuation; Shared.jsx:54 renders only d.photos and its truncated length. enrich_city at server.py:470 counts the entire gallery.
item.expected: Request: 'Quiero poder subir tantas fotografías como quiera' and 'Compartir la ciudad o galería mediante un enlace'. R-030: the share view shows the shared city's photos. Checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: pagination reaches the last record and exposes truncation; counts match the represented rows.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: a city with 201 uploaded photos reports photo_count=201 but its owner gallery can open/edit only the first 200. At 501 photos the public gallery permanently omits the last photo and claims there are 500 files, with no next page or show-all action. Uploads can accumulate past these caps in ordinary batches, so stored and shared travel content becomes inaccessible through the supported galleries. Originals remain stored, but users cannot browse or manage the hidden tail normally.
reproduction_steps: Upload 201 valid photos to one city in several batches.
Open its detail page: the total includes 201, but only 200 gallery items are fetched and no next page exists.
Accumulate 501 photos, issue Compartir galería, and open the link signed out.
Only 500 photos and a 500-file label are returned/displayed; there is no way to load the remainder.
item.surface: Private city/trip galleries; signed-out shared city/trip gallery
item.title: Large galleries silently lose their tail from owner and shared views — fixed 200/500-item caps have no pagination

item.evidence: server.py:638 iterates files[:50] without rejecting or reporting the remaining files, then :641 returns success. AddCityDialog.jsx:42 uploads the full selected files array and :43 reports the city saved without comparing uploaded and selected counts. uploadFiles in lib/api.js:45 appends every selected file.
item.expected: Request: multiple simultaneous photo uploads and 'Subir tantas fotografías como quiera'. Checklist, Files, media and generated artifacts: batches must visibly report rejected/skipped input rather than claim complete success. Either accept the selection or clearly reject/identify the excess and preserve an actionable retry.
item.observed: Files, media and generated artifacts: selecting 51 otherwise valid images in Añadir ciudad saves the city and first 50 images, silently ignores image 51, and closes the dialog with a success toast. That traveller reasonably believes the selected memories were all stored. The omitted original can be reuploaded if the user notices, so this is recoverable content loss rather than destruction of originals.
reproduction_steps: Open Añadir ciudad and select a city.
Select 51 valid images in Fotografías.
Save the city.
The response and stored gallery contain only the first 50; the dialog closes with a saved message and no skipped-file warning.
item.title: Saving a city silently drops photos after the first 50 selected — the upload loop slices the batch and returns success

item.evidence: server.py:526 reads a snapshot with own_city, :528-530 validates the proposed dates against that snapshot, then :545 updates only by {'id': city_id}, with no version or date precondition. CityEditDialog.jsx:19 submits an edit and other API callers can submit partial fields as allowed by CityUpdate.
item.expected: R-032 (derived): submitted dates must be validated against stored dates and invalid updates refused whole. Checklist, Data, persistence and APIs: concurrent updates must preserve the business invariant. Independently, an interval must satisfy end_date >= visit_date in the final stored record, not just in each caller's old snapshot.
item.observed: Data, persistence and APIs: start with 2026-06-01 through 2026-06-10. A partial update setting the start to June 9 and another setting the end to June 2 can both read the original record and independently pass validation. Since their final writes have no conditional guard, both succeed and persist June 9 through June 2, an invalid interval that the new validation promises to prevent. A traveller editing from concurrent clients must manually repair the dates; this is a conditional interleaving, not a runtime observation.
reproduction_steps: Create a city with visit_date=2026-06-01 and end_date=2026-06-10.
In parallel, submit PUT updates setting only visit_date=2026-06-09 and only end_date=2026-06-02.
Arrange for both own_city reads to finish before either update write.
Both validations pass against the old interval, but the final interval ends before it starts.
item.title: Concurrent valid-looking city edits can store an end date before the start — date validation and writes use an unguarded snapshot

item.evidence: public_trip_or_404 at server.py:900 checks only {'id': trip_id, 'is_public': True}, not the owner's profile visibility. Both GET comments (:916-920) and POST comments/likes (:906-928) depend on it. TripDialog.jsx:74 promises 'Visible para otros viajeros si tu perfil es público'; public_profile at server.py:799 actually rejects private owners, so the detail interaction routes enforce a different boundary.
item.expected: Request: 'Perfil privado' and each user decides what to share. Checklist, Auth, sessions and access control: access restrictions must follow the same object across details, mutations and cached/delegated references. The trip control explicitly conditions ordinary social visibility on a public profile; independent share tokens are a separate deliberate access path.
item.observed: Auth, sessions and access control: a viewer who noted a trip id while its owner was public can keep fetching all social comments after that owner makes the profile private, and any signed-in viewer can still add comments or likes. The owner no longer appears on the public-profile route, but the record's interaction routes never check that privacy decision. Scope is previously known public-trip ids; this is not an arbitrary-id discovery claim.
reproduction_steps: Publish a trip through a public profile and note its trip id as another viewer.
Make the owner's profile private, keeping the trip's publish toggle on.
As the viewer, request that trip's social comments: they remain accessible.
While signed in as the viewer, add a comment or like: the route still accepts it despite the now-private profile.
item.title: Making a profile private does not stop access to its trip comments or interactions — social routes check only the trip flag

item.evidence: MiMundo.jsx:138 gives the country-info DialogContent no max-height or overflow scrolling; :147 adds a 160px image, :149-150 adds stats and :152 renders the full unbounded description above :154-156 action controls. The shared DialogContent at components/ui/dialog.jsx:29-38 is fixed and vertically centered with an absolute top-right close button. In contrast, AddCountryDialog.jsx:48 explicitly adds max-h-[92vh] overflow-y-auto. The backend accepts descriptions up to 2000 characters (server.py:253).
item.expected: Request: design must work on Android/iPhone/tablet/computer. Checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: containment, scrolling and reachable controls must hold for long content on supported small viewports. A tall country panel must scroll within the viewport while retaining usable dismissal/actions.
item.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: source predicts that opening a visited country's information panel on a short mobile viewport with a photo and a near-limit multi-paragraph description creates a centered fixed dialog taller than the screen. Its upper content/close control and lower country/edit/delete controls can lie outside the viewport, and the dialog has no internal scroll region. Travellers cannot read/use the full panel normally; dismissing it and opening the country through Mis países is a safe but indirect recovery. This is a layout prediction, not a measured browser result.
reproduction_steps: Save a visited country with a photo and a description near 2000 characters.
On a small phone or short landscape viewport, open that country's panel by clicking the globe.
The panel grows beyond the viewport; attempt to scroll within it to the top close button and bottom actions.
Unlike the add/edit dialog, this panel has no max-height/overflow-y-auto containment.
item.surface: Mi Mundo globe country-info dialog on mobile with long description
item.title: Long country descriptions push mobile panel controls off screen — the fixed country-info dialog has no height limit or scrolling

item.evidence: WorldGlobe.jsx:101 creates a div; :104 and :107 assign only onclick for city labels and country pins. :109 sets pointer-events and cursor, but no tabIndex, role or keyboard handler is set; the descendants are spans/images rather than buttons or links. MiMundo.jsx:72 wires these pointer-only city labels to /ciudades/:id navigation.
item.expected: Checklist, Layout, theme, visuals and UX: shared interaction must work for keyboard and assistive use; checklist, UI state, navigation and interaction: a navigation reference must reach its intended destination. Use keyboard-operable links/buttons or equivalent focus and activation behavior for globe labels.
item.observed: Layout, theme, visuals and UX: keyboard-only travellers cannot focus or activate the city-label or tiny-country flag-pin shortcuts shown on the globe. The onclick handlers work only through pointer activation, with no focusable semantic control. The same records remain reachable from Mis ciudades/Mis países, so this is a minor shortcut-accessibility failure rather than total loss of the core logging task.
reproduction_steps: Open Mi Mundo and zoom in so saved city labels appear.
Use Tab to try to focus a city label, then Enter to open its city.
The div is absent from keyboard navigation and has no keyboard activation handler.
Use Mis ciudades instead to reach the record through the alternative supported route.
item.surface: WorldGlobe city labels and country flag pins
item.title: Keyboard users cannot activate globe city labels or flag pins — clickable divs have no focus or keyboard behavior

reason: The request independently permits sharing individual trips, and the UI describes the country/city privacy switches as controlling the profile's globe, country list and visited-city section. Public-trip country fields and visible achievements are not sufficient to prove that this intentionally separate publication violates the promised privacy policy. Removing this finding rather than assuming global suppression overrides individually published content.
